Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 37268 of 2024
Applicant :- Shyamu

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Shri Ashish Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.K. Srivastava, learned Aga
for the State.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant to quash the Complaint
Case No.163 of 2021 (Janki Vs. Shyamu), under Sections 376, 504, 506 Ipc, Police
Station-Ghughali, District-Maharajganj, presently pending in the Court of the learned Additional
Chief Judicial Magistrate/Additional Civil Judge (Senior Division), District-Maharajganj as well as
summoning order dated 11.9.2023.

3. The case of the applicant is that a complaint was lodged by the opposite party no. 2 who happens
to be the complainant/ victim with an allegation that on 15.09.2020 when the opposite party no. 2/
victim had gone to answer nature's call then the applicant herein pounced upon the opposite party
no. 2 and dragged her to the sugarcane field and thereafter committed to bad act and when the said
incident was narrated to the family members of the opposite party no. 2 then they approached the
family members of the applicant wherein assurance was extended that the opposite party no. 2's

mariage would be solemnized with the applicant, however, on 22.12.2020 at 10.00 when the opposite party no. 2 conceived then pressure was mounted then the applicant along with the co-accused in the complaint hurled abuses and with the help of fist and leg they assualted.
Post sending of complaint through registered post to the police, the complaint was lodged on 08.01.2021.

The statement of the victim/ opposite party no. 2 was recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C.
followedby Samaharu, Kusum and Nikku under Section 202 Cr.P.C., the applicant has been summoned under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC on 11.08.2023.
4.
Questioning the said order, the applicant has been filed the present application.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has not committed the said offence as the entire complaint consist of bundle of lies which have got no nexus with reality for the simple reason that in the complaint, the complainant has depicted herself to be an unmarried woman who was assured solemnization of the marriage with the applicant herein but while drawing attention towards page 56, it is contended that there happens to be a marriage invitation card depicting that the opposite party no. 2's marriage was being solemnized with Chandrash.

He further invited attention of the Court towards the proceedings initiated under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. by the opposite party o. 2 against Chandrash before the Court of Principal Judge/ Family Court,
Maharajganj, being Case No. 516 of 2020 in which the date of the marriage was 15.06.2020 and the said application came to be rejected on account of non-prosecution on 09.09.2021.

entities.text:

Maharajganj

sentences.text: Further submission is that there are material contradictions in the statements of the witnesses vis-a-vis the complaint, in particular, for instance in the statements of Nikku, the incident of committing of offence is stated to be on 15.09.2020 at 5-6 in the morning.
However, in the complaint, there is no date mentioned in that regard.

He further submits that totally false and frivolous allegations have been leveled and the learned Magistrate before summoning the applicant has not applied his mind and, however, looking into the sections under which, the complaint has been lodged, the applicant has been summoned in a mechanical manner.
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the victim was not subjected to medical examination and in case, she was medically examined, the truth could have been surfaced and, thus,
adverse inference is to be drawn against the opposite party no. 2 so as to completely demolish the prosecution theory.

7. Learned AGA on the other hand submits that what would be relevant at the stage of summoning,
would be the allegations in the complaint, vis-a-vis the statements under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.

Learned AGA further submits that once the statements of the witnesses under Section 200 read with Section 202 Cr.P.C. are not in variations or inconsistent with allegations then the Court may not throttle the investigation at this stage.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the records carefully.
9. Apparently, in the present case in hand, at the instance of the applicant, this Court is confronted with the challenge raised to the summoning order.
There are certain criterias which have to be adopted in determining as to whether the summoning order suffers from legal infirmity or not.

sentences.text: 2 Amongst others one of the criterias would be the nature of the allegations contained in the complaint vis-a-vis the statements under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.

In case, there are material contradictions or variations in the statements vis-a-vis the complaint and it is found that even on prima facie basis, the case is frivolous and not triable then the the Court in extraordinary circumstances bestows its consideration and interferes in that regard.
10.

Applying the said factors in the present facts and the circumstances of the case, the Court finds that the victim herein had alleged that the applicant herein had outraged her modesty 15.09.2020 when the victim had gone to answers nature's call.
Further allegation is that on 22.12.2020 when the victim became pregnant then pressure was being mounted for getting the marriage of the applicant solemnized with the opposite party no. 2.
The statement under Section 200 Cr.P.C. of the victim- Samaharu, Kusum and Nikku under Section 202 Cr.P.C. stick to the allegations of committing of bad act on 15.09.2020.

Though the learned counsel for the applicant may be right to certain extent that the Nikku in her statements under Section 202 Cr.P.C. had spelled out that the bat act was committed on 15.09.2020 at 5-6 in the morning but the same is not the recital in the complaint,
however, the same cannot be a ground to out-rightly overrule the possibility of the commission of the offence.
What the Court is required at this stage when challenge has been raised to the summoning order is the fact as to whether the case is triable or not.
More importantly, the victim sticks to the allegations.

11. As regards, the submission of the counsel for the applicant is that the victim was not subjected to medical examination is concerned, thus, the same would be of no aid or help at the stage of summoning, particularly, when the effect of non-medical examination of the victim would be tested and its own strength at the time when the trial commences and a decision is to be taken as to whether the accused is to be acquitted or convicted.

12. More so, the allegations of the applicant is that opposite party no. 2 was already married on the date when the complaint was lodged and also the proceedings under Section 125 the Cr.P.C. was initiated which came to be rejected on 09.09.2021, thus, the prosecution theory of commission of bad act is out-rightly overruled is concerned, this Court is not required to go into the said issue at this stage, as the same would have its own import and effect and ramification when the trial commences.

13. Looking into the fact and circumstances of the case, from the four corners of law and bearing in mind, the Hon'ble Apex Court in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.PC./ 528 BNSS, this Court does not find the present case to be an exceptional case for warranting interference.
14. In view of the said discussion, no case is made out.
Accordingly, the application stands dismissed.
15. In the opinion of the Court, once a bail application is preferred then the same shall be considered with most expeditions strictly as per the law of the land without any delay.
